title: A western oxygen transfer fit did not beat a trend in four CalCOFI time blocks from 2001 to 2020
abstract: A published positive transfer with western North Pacific oxygen delays of 5-25 years improved one later CalCOFI test. We tested the same model across four five-year time blocks and against two source timing controls. The model trains from 1984 through 2000, 2005, 2010 and 2015. On 2001-2020, its pooled RMS error was 5.71 umol/kg, against 4.94 for a target linear trend and 5.66 for persistence. Each control retained the western linear trend and changed source residual timing. All kernels were refit for each of 499 random-phase and 499 eight-year block controls. The observed gain over the target trend did not pass either test (p = 0.278 and 0.270). We reproduced the original 2007-2020 error of 6.25 against trend error 7.55, but that gain also did not pass the controls (p = 0.176 and 0.190). We show that a linear source gives no delay information when the model has a free offset. These results limit the predictive evidence for this fitted transfer. They do not exclude a physical route or the outcrop mechanism. Tests use published annual aggregate indices with full-record processing, interpolated source gaps, and conditional stationary-residual nulls. No new raw observations are used. Code, exact aggregate inputs, provenance, predictions and all null scores are included.

display.caption: Four frozen five-year tests and source timing controls. The blue line marks observed skill relative to a target linear trend. Positive skill is better.
